candidate_relations.reason: The immunophenotype (CD138+, CD56+, CD20-, PAX5-, EBV+) with plasmablastic differentiation and FISH gains at BCL6, MYC, and IGH loci are characteristic of plasmablastic lymphoma, not extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma. NK/T-cell lymphoma would typically be CD3+, CD56+, cytotoxic marker-positive, and would not show CD138 positivity or IGH rearrangement. While both are EBV-positive and can present in the nasal cavity, the immunophenotype and molecular findings firmly distinguish PBL from NK/T-cell lymphoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Different lymphoma subtype; EBV-positive and nasal location overlap but immunophenotype and FISH findings are incompatible

case_quality_flags: HIV-negative PBL is atypical but well-documented; EBV positivity and plasmablastic immunophenotype with MYC/IGH gains support the reference diagnosis
CD56 positivity in PBL can create diagnostic overlap with NK/T-cell lymphoma, but CD138+/CD20-/PAX5- profile resolves the distinction
